observation_summary: The TimeSeries.createCopy method throws an IllegalArgumentException when the calculated range is invalid (start > end), even when the input range is logically empty. The system should return an empty series instead of crashing.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an insufficient validation condition. The original code only checked if 'endIndex < 0' to determine if the range was empty. The fix adds a necessary check '(endIndex < startIndex)' to correctly identify cases where the calculated range is invalid/empty, preventing the subsequent call to createCopy(startIndex, endIndex) from triggering an IllegalArgumentException.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows an IllegalArgumentException: 'Requires start <= end.' originating from TimeSeries.createCopy.
The fix diff adds a condition '|| (endIndex < startIndex)' to the existing 'if (endIndex < 0)' check.
The bug report states: 'Here I would expect an empty serie to be returned, not an exception.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the calculation of indices is part of the method, the root cause is the failure to validate the resulting range before passing it to the next step, which is a classic 'Checking' defect.
